question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}(x+y), & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(Y\le 1).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le 3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{6}(x+y)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+xy]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\frac{1}{2}+y]-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{12}+\frac{y}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{12}+\frac{y}{6}, & 0\le y\le 3, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le 1) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{1}{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{12}+\frac{y}{6})\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{y}{12}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{12}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{12}]-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
